targetAudience.primary: Engineers designing operational interfaces, replay and evidence retention for agent runtimes
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands command transcripts, UI compaction and the difference between logs and formal audit records.
targetAudience.readerProblem: Showing every command overwhelms operators, but destructive summarization can erase the execution detail needed to inspect failures and reconstruct work.

whyNow: A same-day merged Codex TUI change demonstrates bounded grouping of successful commands while retaining individual command and output detail in transcript_lines and applying compatible replay behavior.

externalHook.description: Operational readability improves when routine success is compacted, yet governance weakens if compaction mutates the only evidence-bearing record.

coreProposition: Operational compaction should be a bounded, replayable view transform over recoverable execution evidence, while formal auditability remains a separate durability and provenance contract.

originalValue.description: Separates presentation, evidence and audit models; derives explicit compaction boundaries for failures, interaction, group size, replay and external-effect evidence.

readerTakeaway: Compact routine success only in the view layer, keep detailed events addressable, preserve failures and interaction boundaries, version replay rules and do not label a transcript as an audit log without stronger guarantees.

supported: Only successful Agent and UnifiedExecStartup activity is grouped, with a 32-call bound and several flush boundaries.
Compact display can coexist with retained individual commands and output in transcript_lines.
Replay applies the grouping principle without duplicate starts and overlapping active work remains visible.
uncertain: The transcript's retention and mutation guarantees
How transformation versions should be persisted

firstPartyRole.rationale: The argument concerns general operational UI and evidence-model design and stands without first-party project references.

decisionReason: The source provides a concrete bounded mechanism and the Research Object adds an independently useful three-layer model with explicit non-audit boundaries.
